subject.title: Feature: Inject context window % into system prompt runtime section

question: Should OpenClaw add passive per-turn context-window usage to the core Runtime prompt line, fold it into the broader runtime self-context design, or keep context visibility on explicit status and usage surfaces?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the remaining choice defines a model-facing prompt contract, freshness semantics, and prompt-cache behavior that automation should not pick alone.

options.title: Approve narrow Runtime field
options.body: Add a compact `context=` field sourced only from fresh bounded session usage/window data, below the cache boundary, with tests for unavailable and stale values.

options.title: Fold into runtime self-context
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader runtime self-context layer explicitly covers context-window usage and avoids duplicate prompt surfaces.

options.title: Keep explicit status surfaces only
options.body: Close or re-scope the request after documenting that `/status`, `/context`, `/usage`, and `session_status` are the intended product boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow Runtime field
recommendation.body: Add a compact `context=` field sourced only from fresh bounded session usage/window data, below the cache boundary, with tests for unavailable and stale values.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest combination of recent prompt/runtime code history and prior maintainer-facing review context on this issue cluster.
